description.narrative: "DON'T PUB DROP 1. Why was code established and nature of the work In 1999, the Eastern Nile (EN) riparian's, including Egypt, Ethiopia and Sudan, agreed to establish an investment oriented program referred to as the Eastern Nile Subsidiary Action Program (ENSAP) under the framework of the Nile Basin Initiative (NBI). In 2001, by the EN countries reached consensus that the first ENSAP 'project' , referred to as the Integrated Development of the Eastern Nile (IDEN) project, would ""initiate a regional, integrated, multipurpose development project through a first set of investments to confer tangible benefits# and demonstrate joint action."" This first set of agreed investments included 7 'subprojects: ' - Irrigation & Drainage - Ethiopia-Sudan Interconnections - Flood Preparedness and Early Warning - Watershed Management - EN Power Trade Investment studies - EN Planning Model - Baro-Akobo multipurpose water resources development The IDEN Facilitation code was established in FY02 to provide technical assistance to the EN Regional Technical Office (ENTRO), a newly formed sub-regional NBI project office for the Eastern Nile, and facilitate project preparation activities, as well as support institutional development to their nascent office. In parallel to the Bank-executed IDEN Facilitation code, a PHRD grant of $1.5 million (2003-2007) was obtained for client-executed activities related to project preparation, particularly related to the EN Planning Model, Flood Preparedness, and the Ethiopia-Sudan Interconnection. Client-executed project preparation activities were also supplemented by GEF and NBTF-financed grants to ENTRO for watershed management and other IDEN activities. Some projects, such as the Power Trade studies, where supported bilaterally by other Partners (i.e., AfDB). The IDEN Facilitation supported Bank staff (Bank, co-term, etc) and consultants, and related expenses (travel, workshops, technical consultancies, etc), required to facilitate dialogue and build consensus among the EN countries, assist in institutional development of ENTRO, and to support and review project preparation activities. An integrated approach was required in the early years, the historic tensions among these countries, the need to build harmonized project preparation approaches for this new entity, and riparian preference. 2. Why the code was closed As ENTRO matured and project preparation activities advanced, a decision was made to 'spin -off' IDEN 'subprojects' as individual projects, with individual preparation and/or lending codes. As projects were ready and alternative funding mechanisms were put in place, all IDEN projects were 'spun off.' This included separate codes for investment oriented projects (and associated project preparation related activities), as well as for institutional strengthening (and associated 'facilitation' and institutional strengthening activities). The IDEN Facilitation code was last used in FY05."
